correctness.rationale: Explicit enumerated domain comprises all 2^15-1=32767 candidate nonempty faces; exact support predicate leaves 710, with face vector (15,105,260,225,90,15). Verified 345 pair Morse matching with one critical 0-cell and 19 critical 2-cells; complete directed Hasse-sort visits 710 of 710 vertices across 2430 arrows, establishing concentration, connectedness, rank19. For each of 11 S6 conjugacy classes enumerate all fixed oriented simplex traces, compute Hopf character χ_H2=Σ(-1)^j tr_Cj−1 (valid as H0 trivial and other reduced H_i=0). Trace vector [-1,-1,1,1,1,1,1,-1,-1,-5,19]. Murnaghan–Nakayama generates orthogonal 11×11 irreducible S6 table and exact inner products m=1 for partitions (3,1,1,1),(2,2,1,1), else 0. Independent script uses a different 32767-subset construction, exact ranks over p=2,3,5 and Young-rule character table/Kostka inversion, confirming same multiplicities. Character-zero and rational Specht realization follow by standard symmetric-group representation theory. The non-equivariant wedge is prior literature, not novelty.

originality.rationale: The closest exact-graph theorem (Nilakantan–Singh, arXiv:1802.05848v1 Theorem 1.3) establishes the rank-19 non-equivariant homotopy type, but does not compute the canonical full S6 homology representation. value.rationale: The full six-point permutation action is canonical for the graph and its complex; the nineteen sphere multiplicity previously known does not determine its character. Giving the exact decomposition into two inequivalent dimensions 10 and 9 distinguishes how different permutations act (e.g. a transposition has trace −5), providing a natural small symmetric test case for equivariant topology and character-theoretic methods. A precise structural symmetry invariant, rather than an arbitrary numeric slice or a routine reconfirmation of the published wedge rank, is computed. It is not a theorem for all k and does not imply full equivariant homotopy.
